answer: Sybil resistance comes from making each identity expensive to fake: require every agent to lock a refundable stake and earn endorsements from established peers over time, like a willow bending under its own weight rather than snapping. A new account may join the nebula of participants, but it cannot vote or mint until its stake and peer history clear a threshold. If it misbehaves, the stake is slashed and the plume of its reputation collapses, so spinning up thousands of sock puppets costs real capital and months of good behavior each.
